topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining the learning outcomes, recalling the progression model of tumorigenesis, and setting up the hallmarks of cancer framework.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and pathway mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how oncogenic mutations across cell-surface receptors and downstream cascades drive sustained proliferation and overcome growth-inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Differentiation block in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how malignant transformation can arrest cells in an immature, non-terminally differentiated state while preserving their capacity to divide.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how alterations in p53 regulation and the mitochondrial apoptotic machinery allow cancer cells to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality and cellular senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how telomere shortening and stress signaling enforce senescence, and how cancer cells bypass this barrier by upregulating telomerase.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells shift toward aerobic glycolysis and how metabolic enzyme mutations generate oncometabolites that drive epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the requirement for new blood vessel growth to sustain tumor tissue beyond the diffusion limit of oxygen and the regulatory balance controlling this switch.

topics.label: The metastatic cascade and clonal dissemination
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the multistep progression of metastasis, including circulatory dissemination, diagnostic biomarkers, seed-and-soil interactions, and underlying genomic features.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and practical session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic concludes the presentation with framing comments on recent hallmark literature, expectations for student revision, and directions for upcoming practicals.
